question: Which dynasty defeated the Kanva dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Satavahana Dynasty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Satavahana dynasty (founded by Simuka) defeated/overthrew the Kanva dynasty around 28 BCE, establishing their rule in the Deccan region. (सातवाहन वंश ने कण्व वंश को पराजित किया)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Sequence of Magadha dynasties: Haryanka → Shishunaga → Nanda → Maurya → Shunga → Kanva → Satavahana.

• The Kanva dynasty (founded by Vasudeva Kanva) had itself replaced the Shunga dynasty.

• The most famous Satavahana ruler was Gautamiputra Satakarni.

NOTE

• The Satavahanas issued lead and potin coins, promoted trade, and their inscriptions are an important source of ancient Indian history (e.g., the Nasik Prashasti).

question: Which of the following best represents the Revenue Deficit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Revenue Expenditure – Revenue Receipts.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure − Revenue Receipts. It arises when the government's revenue expenditure exceeds its revenue receipts, meaning it cannot meet even its day-to-day running expenses from its regular income. (राजस्व घाटा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure − Total Receipts (excluding borrowings) = the total borrowing requirement of the government.

• Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit − Interest Payments.

• Effective Revenue Deficit = Revenue Deficit − Grants for creation of capital assets.

NOTE

• Revenue receipts (tax + non-tax) do not create a liability or reduce assets; a revenue deficit is considered undesirable as it implies borrowing for consumption, not investment.

question: The non-metallic mineral mica is used in which of the following industries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Electrical industry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The non-metallic mineral "mica" is widely used in the electrical and electronics industry because it is an excellent insulator — it has high dielectric strength, low power loss and resistance to heat. (अभ्रक — विद्युत उद्योग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• India is one of the largest producers of mica; major deposits are in Jharkhand, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan (the Koderma belt of Jharkhand is famous).

• Mica is also used in making capacitors, insulators and electronic components.

NOTE

• Non-metallic minerals include mica, limestone, gypsum, dolomite and manganese (metallic). Mica's key property for the electrical industry is its insulating (dielectric) capacity.

question: Which virus is responsible for causing AIDS?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome) is caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV). HIV attacks and weakens the body's immune system, specifically the CD4 (helper T) cells, making the body vulnerable to infections. (एड्स — एचआईवी वायरस)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• HIV is a retrovirus and mainly spreads through unprotected sexual contact, contaminated blood/needles, and from an infected mother to child.

• 1 December is observed as World AIDS Day.

NOTE

• HPV causes cervical cancer and warts; HSV causes herpes; Influenza virus causes flu. This is a sensitive health topic; the focus here is purely the factual virus-disease association tested in exams.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India emphasises the participation of workers in the management of industries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 43A.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 43A of the Constitution directs the State to take steps to secure the participation of workers in the management of undertakings/industries. (अनुच्छेद 43A — उद्योगों के प्रबंधन में श्रमिकों की भागीदारी)

• It was added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Article 43A is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), Part IV of the Constitution.

• Related labour DPSPs: Article 39 (adequate means of livelihood, equal pay), Article 41 (right to work), Article 43 (living wage), Article 43B (promotion of cooperatives).

NOTE

• DPSPs are non-justiciable (not enforceable in court) but are "fundamental in the governance of the country" (Article 37). They aim at establishing a welfare state.

question: Which of the following two properties of metals are exploited to prepare very thin sheets of silver to decorate sweets?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Malleability and lustre.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The thin silver sheets (chandi ka varq) used to decorate sweets exploit two metallic properties:

◦ Malleability — the ability of a metal to be beaten/hammered into thin sheets.

◦ Lustre — the shine of the metal, which gives the sweets a decorative, attractive appearance. (आघातवर्धनीयता एवं चमक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Ductility is the ability to be drawn into thin wires (e.g., copper, gold).

• Sonorous means metals produce a ringing sound when struck (used in bells).

NOTE

• Key physical properties of metals: malleability, ductility, lustre, sonorousness, high melting point, and good conductivity of heat and electricity. Gold and silver are the most malleable and ductile metals.

question: What is the quorum of the Lok Sabha at the time of the Presidential address, which is held at the opening of each session of the Lok Sabha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is One-tenth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The quorum (minimum number of members required to conduct business) of the Lok Sabha (and Rajya Sabha) is one-tenth (1/10) of the total number of members of the House, as laid down in Article 100(3) of the Constitution. (गणपूर्ति — कुल सदस्यों का 1/10)

• For the Lok Sabha (545 members), the quorum is therefore about 55 members.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• If there is no quorum, it is the duty of the Speaker/Chairperson to adjourn the House or suspend the meeting until there is a quorum.

• The President addresses both Houses together at the commencement of the first session after each general election and at the start of the first session of each year (Article 87).

NOTE

• Articles on Parliament: 79 (constitution of Parliament), 80 (Rajya Sabha), 81 (Lok Sabha), 100 (voting and quorum).

question: As of July 2023, who was the Member of Parliament from the parliamentary constituency of Varanasi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narendra Modi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of July 2023, Narendra Modi, the Prime Minister of India, was the Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha) from the Varanasi parliamentary constituency in Uttar Pradesh. (वाराणसी — नरेंद्र मोदी)

• He was first elected from Varanasi in 2014 and re-elected in 2019 and 2024.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Varanasi (Kashi/Banaras) is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, situated on the banks of the Ganga, and a major religious and cultural centre.

• Rajnath Singh represents Lucknow; Smriti Irani represented Amethi (2019).

NOTE

• The Lok Sabha is directly elected by the people; a candidate must be at least 25 years old to contest a Lok Sabha seat.

question: The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College in Aligarh was founded by __________.
option_4: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Kalam'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/Kalam.ttf') format('truetype');} </style>Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sir Syed Ahmed Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) College at Aligarh was founded in 1875 by Sir Syed Ahmed Khan, a social reformer and educationist, to promote modern, Western-style education among Indian Muslims. (सर सैयद अहमद खान — एमएओ कॉलेज)

• This later grew into the Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) in 1920.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sir Syed Ahmed Khan started the Aligarh Movement for the social and educational upliftment of Muslims.

• He also wrote "Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind" (The Causes of the Indian Revolt of 1857).

NOTE

• Other important educational institutions: Banaras Hindu University (BHU) by Madan Mohan Malaviya (1916), Jamia Millia Islamia (1920).

question: Panch Mahal, a palace in Fatehpur Sikri, was built by the Mughal Emperor __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Akbar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Panch Mahal, a five-storeyed palace in Fatehpur Sikri, was built by the Mughal Emperor Akbar. It is an open, column-based pavilion, each storey smaller than the one below, used for relaxation and enjoying the breeze. (पंच महल — अकबर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri (near Agra) and made it his capital for a time; it is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

• Other structures at Fatehpur Sikri: the Buland Darwaza (built to commemorate the Gujarat victory), the Jama Masjid, Diwan-i-Khas, Diwan-i-Aam and the tomb of Salim Chishti.

NOTE

• Akbar (1556–1605) followed a policy of religious tolerance (Sulh-i-Kul), introduced Din-i-Ilahi, and abolished the Jizya (tax on non-Muslims).

question: The Jhaveri Sisters are known for keeping alive the temple tradition of which of the following classical dances of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipuri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Jhaveri Sisters (Nayana, Ranjana, Suverna and Darshana Jhaveri) are renowned for reviving and keeping alive the Manipuri classical dance tradition. (मणिपुरी नृत्य — झावेरी सिस्टर्स)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Manipuri dance, from Manipur, is known for its gentle, graceful and fluid movements, and themes based on Radha–Krishna (Raslila) and Vaishnavism.

• The dancers wear a distinctive stiff, decorated skirt called the "Kumil".

NOTE

• Classical dances and their states: Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kathak (North India), Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha).

question: The historical novel, 'Train to Pakistan' was written by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khushwant Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Train to Pakistan" (1956) is a famous historical novel written by Khushwant Singh. It vividly depicts the horrors and human tragedy of the Partition of India in 1947 through the fictional village of Mano Majra. (ट्रेन टू पाकिस्तान — खुशवंत सिंह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Khushwant Singh was a noted author, journalist and Padma Vibhushan awardee; his other works include "Delhi: A Novel" and "The Company of Women".

• Other Partition literature: "Tamas" (Bhisham Sahni), "Ice-Candy-Man / Cracking India" (Bapsi Sidhwa).

NOTE

• Author–book pairs for SSC: The God of Small Things (Arundhati Roy), The Great Indian Novel (Shashi Tharoor), The Discovery of India (Jawaharlal Nehru).

question: The Indravati National Park is located in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indravati National Park is located in the Bijapur district of Chhattisgarh, on the banks of the Indravati River. It is one of the finest and best-known wildlife reserves of the state and is also a Tiger Reserve. (इंद्रावती राष्ट्रीय उद्यान — छत्तीसगढ़)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Indravati National Park is famous for the wild buffalo and the rare Barasingha (swamp deer), along with tigers, leopards and gaur.

• Other national parks in Chhattisgarh: Kanger Valley and Guru Ghasidas (Sanjay) National Park.

NOTE

• The Indravati River is a tributary of the Godavari. India has over 100 national parks; the first was Jim Corbett (1936, Uttarakhand).

question: Emani Sankara Sastry and Doraiswamy Iyengar are both associated with which musical instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Veena.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Emani Sankara Sastry and Mysore Doraiswamy Iyengar were both eminent maestros of the Veena, a classical stringed instrument of India. (वीणा वादक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Veena (Saraswati Veena) is one of the oldest Indian instruments, closely associated with Carnatic music and the goddess Saraswati.

• It is a plucked string instrument known for its rich, resonant tone.

NOTE

• Instrument–artist pairs: Veena (S. Balachander, Doraiswamy Iyengar), Flute (Hariprasad Chaurasia), Sitar (Ravi Shankar), Sarod (Amjad Ali Khan), Shehnai (Bismillah Khan), Ghatam (Vikku Vinayakram).

question: According to the census of India 2011, which of the following states is least urbanised?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census 2011, among the given options Himachal Pradesh was the least urbanised state, with only about 10% of its population living in urban areas. (हिमाचल प्रदेश — न्यूनतम शहरीकृत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Himachal Pradesh had the lowest urbanisation among all Indian states (about 10%), followed by Bihar (about 11%).

• The most urbanised state was Goa (about 62%); among UTs, Delhi and Chandigarh are almost fully urban.

NOTE

• India's overall urban population in 2011 was about 31.16%. Urbanisation is measured as the percentage of population living in towns/cities.

question: Consider the following pairs (Work – Writer): 1. Rajtaringini – Kalhan   2. Gita Govinda – Chandbardai   3. Vikramarjuna-Vijaya – Pampa. Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 3.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pair 1 is correct: "Rajatarangini" (a chronicle of the kings of Kashmir) was written by Kalhana.

• Pair 3 is correct: "Vikramarjuna Vijaya" (also called Pampa Bharata) was written by Pampa, the great Kannada poet (Adikavi).

• Pair 2 is WRONG: "Gita Govinda" was written by Jayadeva, not Chandbardai. (Chand Bardai wrote the "Prithviraj Raso".)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2 (pairs 1 and 3).

Additional Information

• Rajatarangini (12th century) is considered one of the earliest works of historical writing in India.

• Pampa is called the "Adikavi" (first poet) of Kannada literature.

NOTE

• Famous work–author pairs: Prithviraj Raso (Chand Bardai), Gita Govinda (Jayadeva), Harshacharita/Kadambari (Banabhatta), Mudrarakshasa (Vishakhadatta).

question: The navigable portion of Barak River in India is the 121 km stretch between Lakhipur and Bhanga, which was declared as _______ in the year 2016.
solution_text:
The correct answer is NW-16.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 121 km navigable stretch of the Barak River between Lakhipur and Bhanga was declared as National Waterway 16 (NW-16) in 2016. (बराक नदी — राष्ट्रीय जलमार्ग-16)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Barak River flows through Assam and is important for the Barak Valley region.

• Major National Waterways: NW-1 (Ganga: Prayagraj–Haldia), NW-2 (Brahmaputra: Dhubri–Sadiya), NW-3 (West Coast Canal, Kerala).

NOTE

• National Waterways are declared under the National Waterways Act, 2016, and managed by the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) for cheap and eco-friendly water transport.

question: Against which of the following were 'Swadeshi' and 'Boycott' used as the means of protest and struggle, for the first time in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Partition of Bengal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The methods of "Swadeshi" (using Indian-made goods) and "Boycott" (of British goods and institutions) were first adopted on a large scale during the anti-Partition of Bengal agitation (1905), launched against Lord Curzon's partition of Bengal. (बंगाल विभाजन — स्वदेशी एवं बहिष्कार आंदोलन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Swadeshi Movement promoted Indian industries, national education and the use of khadi.

• The Partition of Bengal (1905) was finally annulled in 1911.

NOTE

• Later, Mahatma Gandhi used Swadeshi and Boycott in the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920). Leaders of the Swadeshi movement included Bipin Chandra Pal, Lala Lajpat Rai and Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Lal-Bal-Pal).

question: A hockey ground is rectangular in shape, measuring 91.4 m in length and _______ in width.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 55 m.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A standard field hockey ground is rectangular, measuring 91.4 metres (100 yards) in length and 55 metres (60 yards) in width. (हॉकी मैदान — 91.4 मी × 55 मी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Hockey is often regarded as India's national game (unofficially); India won 8 Olympic gold medals in hockey (six in a row from 1928 to 1956).

• Major Dhyan Chand is called the "Wizard of Hockey"; his birthday (29 August) is National Sports Day.

NOTE

• Playing-area dimensions for SSC: Hockey (91.4 m × 55 m), Football (length 100–110 m), Cricket pitch (22 yards ≈ 20.12 m).

question:
The National Population Register was created under the provisions of _______ and _______.

a. the Citizenship Act, 1965   b. the Citizenship Rules, 2004   c. the Citizenship Act, 1955   d. the Citizenship Rules, 2003
solution_text:
The correct answer is c; d (the Citizenship Act, 1955 and the Citizenship Rules, 2003).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Population Register (NPR) was created under the provisions of the Citizenship Act, 1955 and the Citizenship (Registration of Citizens and Issue of National Identity Cards) Rules, 2003. (एनपीआर — नागरिकता अधिनियम 1955 एवं नियम 2003)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The NPR is a register of the usual residents of the country (a person who has resided in a local area for at least 6 months or intends to stay for the next 6 months).

• It is prepared at the local, sub-district, district, state and national levels, under the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (Ministry of Home Affairs).

NOTE

• The NPR is different from the NRC (National Register of Citizens) — the NPR records residents, while the NRC is meant to record citizens.

question: In May 2023, the Supreme Court interpreted which article related to the governance structure of Delhi, which outlines the principles of federalism, participatory democracy and collective responsibility?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 239AA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In May 2023, the Supreme Court interpreted Article 239AA, which deals with the special governance structure of the National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi. The Court ruled on the division of powers between the elected Delhi government and the Lieutenant Governor, upholding principles of federalism, participatory democracy and collective responsibility. (अनुच्छेद 239AA — दिल्ली की शासन संरचना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Article 239AA (inserted by the 69th Amendment, 1991) gave Delhi a Legislative Assembly and a Council of Ministers, but kept land, police and public order with the Centre.

• The 2023 verdict held that the Delhi government has control over services (except the three reserved subjects), though this was later modified by an ordinance/law.

NOTE

• Article 243B relates to Panchayats; Article 323A to Administrative Tribunals; Article 226 to the writ jurisdiction of High Courts.

question: Nishagandhi festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Nishagandhi Dance and Music Festival is celebrated in Kerala, at the Nishagandhi open-air auditorium in Thiruvananthapuram. It showcases India's classical dance and music forms. (निशागंधी महोत्सव — केरल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The festival is organised by the Kerala Tourism Department and features leading classical artists from across India.

• Other festivals of Kerala: Onam (harvest festival), Thrissur Pooram (temple festival) and Vishu.

NOTE

• Kerala, "God's Own Country", is famous for its backwaters, Ayurveda, and the classical arts Kathakali and Mohiniyattam.

question: Which Bharatanatyam dancer is the recipient of one of India's top civilian award, the Padma Vibhushan 1977?
solution_text:
The correct answer is T Balasaraswati.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tanjore Balasaraswati (T. Balasaraswati), the legendary Bharatanatyam dancer, was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 1977. She was renowned worldwide for her expressive abhinaya and played a major role in popularising Bharatanatyam globally. (टी. बालासरस्वती — पद्म विभूषण 1977)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• She had earlier received the Padma Bhushan (1957) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, one of the oldest and based on the Natya Shastra.

NOTE

• Kelucharan Mohapatra was an Odissi maestro; Yamini Krishnamurthy and Mallika Sarabhai are noted Bharatanatyam/Kuchipudi dancers of a later generation.

question: Where was the inaugural season of Ultimate Kho-Kho League held in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pune.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The inaugural season of the Ultimate Kho-Kho (UKK) League was held in 2022 in Pune, Maharashtra. Odisha Juggernauts won the first title. (अल्टीमेट खो-खो लीग — 2022, पुणे)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kho-Kho is a traditional Indian tag/pursuit sport played between two teams; it, along with Kabaddi, is a popular indigenous game.

• The Ultimate Kho-Kho League is a franchise-based professional league aimed at popularising the sport.

NOTE

• India hosted the first Kho-Kho World Cup in 2025 (New Delhi), with the Indian men's and women's teams winning the titles.

question:
Which of the following options correctly matches Column-A (Cell organelles) with Column-B (Function)?

i. Cell membrane   ii. Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum   iii. Golgi apparatus   iv. Ribosomes  |  a. Protein synthesis  b. Important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids  c. Synthesis of lipid  d. Transport of the molecules
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-d, ii-c, iii-b, iv-a.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct matching of cell organelles with their functions is:

◦ i. Cell membrane → d. Transport of the molecules (it regulates the movement of substances in and out of the cell — it is "selectively permeable").

◦ ii. Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum → c. Synthesis of lipid (the smooth ER makes lipids and steroids).

◦ iii. Golgi apparatus → b. Important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids (it modifies, packages and dispatches materials).

◦ iv. Ribosomes → a. Protein synthesis (ribosomes are the site of protein manufacture).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1 (i-d, ii-c, iii-b, iv-a).

Additional Information

• The Rough ER (with ribosomes) helps in protein synthesis and transport; the Golgi apparatus is called the "post office of the cell".

• Mitochondria are the "powerhouse of the cell"; lysosomes are the "suicidal bags".

NOTE

• The cell is the structural and functional unit of life. Ribosomes are the only organelle also found in prokaryotes (bacteria), which lack membrane-bound organelles.
